scope: Diagnostic research only. No post-process or second scorer changes the emitted ASR final, enters the AR1M3 comparison, or receives qualification credit.

scaffold.fake_vad: Caller-supplied speech labels exercise ordered speech-start, speech-end, reset, and cancel transitions without claiming acoustic VAD behavior.
scaffold.fake_second_pass_scorer: Injected deterministic scores exercise top-one fallback and N-best selection while returning only transcript hashes and leaving the final unchanged.

observed_m1_adapter_surface.wenet_boundary: The tested sherpa-onnx online CTC conversions do not establish native WeNet U2++ attention rescoring.

potential_directions.value_hypothesis: Normalize stable spacing, punctuation, number, and English-token presentation after preserving the raw final.
potential_directions.risk: A rule may alter semantic content or hide model errors; score raw and normalized forms separately.

potential_directions.value_hypothesis: Product vocabulary may benefit from audited entity normalization or decoder-side contextual bias.
potential_directions.risk: Context bias is decoder behavior, not interchangeable with post-processing, and may harm general utterances.

potential_directions.value_hypothesis: A scorer can only recover an alternative that the first pass exposes.
potential_directions.risk: A different decoder/runtime path, reproducible score identity, latency, RSS, and genuine N-best output are prerequisites.

potential_directions.value_hypothesis: Endpoint timing may reduce speech-end-to-final delay without altering ASR text.
potential_directions.risk: VAD truncation can damage first or last syllables; endpoint latency and ASR decode cost must remain separate.

m2_boundary: Only small development-data diagnostics may follow. No real post-process enters the formal comparison, and no direction is an M2 advance or qualification decision.
